Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB474.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liaozong of Panshan. Liaozong Chaojian owns the retained deployment: gathering, with spring grass deep and autumn leaves falling, the mountains, rivers, great earth, grasses, trees and groves, the sentient and the insentient, into one body — pick it up and use it, nothing not permitted — then raising Zhaozhou's cypress tree to show what that picking-up is.

Senses.Explanation: The sentient and the insentient. Zhongfeng Mingben, unfolding the ancestor's tag that the true-suchness dharma-realm has no self and no other, grants the doctrinal readers their point — mountains, rivers, the great earth, sentient and insentient, none of it obtainable as being — then turns their own gold-and-vessel image on them: gold is the substance, pots and hairpins are provisional names, and meeting the provisional in the substance, the false names melt unexpelled. Yuanwu Keqin, at a funeral hall, rolls the address out — every buddha present, and more: all sentient and insentient things through the boundless oceans of scent, past, present and future, stilled and changeless, their crossing lights woven like a net of jewel-threads — then asks what power the departed lady leans on, and answers with the earth shaking to greet Mahasthamaprapta and flowers filling the sky to send off Guanyin. Huanyou Zhengchuan holds up the great pure mani-pearl, bright inside and out, nothing it fails to light: from buddha-ancestors and bodhi, nirvana, suchness and prajna above, to the hells and hungry ghosts below, every dharma of both worlds, the shadows of sentient and insentient things and dharmas across the ten directions are all mirrored in this pearl — then dares the assembly to find where the shadow is once root and dust no longer couple. Hanyue Fazang, unwilling to let the stone lie silent under the pines, hands the preaching to the myriad appearances — clouds and mists, water striking stone, Mount Sumeru's body and the long broad tongue — with today's ten directions for a mouth: mountains speak, waters speak, emptiness speaks, being speaks, lands speak, dusts speak, the sentient and insentient of the three times all turning the wheel together, so that hearer and seer stand on the spot as buddhas. Tianran Hanshi reads Yunyan's long silence as the whole of it: across the ten directions and the three times, every principle, every affair, the sentient and the insentient, dharma and non-dharma — not one escapes that one long silence, while eyes that waver have no part in it. Gulin Zhi, hauled out to the seat by the official Mu, pulls the thing Bodhidharma's nine years could not pierce and three hundred assemblies could not say — the one treasure hidden in form-mountain — and offers it to the assembly and to the sentient and insentient of the whole great earth: one eye sees, one ear hears, one enjoyment. Zhufeng Huanmin counts the whole ledger in triads — the noble and base, dead and alive, true and conventional, male and female, sentient and insentient, human and non-human of past, future and present all fixedly become buddha — then asks for the line where each, already buddha, turns merit into place. And Liaozong Chaojian, with spring grass deep and autumn leaves falling, wind in the trees and water lifting the boat, gathers mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses and trees and groves, the sentient and the insentient, into one body — pick it up and use it, nothing not permitted — then raises Zhaozhou's cypress tree to show what that picking-up is.
